issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and that the appeal, motion for new trial, and amendments were timely and properly filed.

issues.label: Preservation of issues
issues.why: The court must determine whether each claim was raised and ruled on below or is otherwise procedurally defaulted.

issues.label: Standard of review: sufficiency
issues.why: The court must apply Jackson v. Virginia, viewing evidence in the light most favorable to the verdict and deferring to the jury on credibility.

issues.label: Elements of malice murder
issues.why: The court must ensure the evidence proved an unlawful killing with malice aforethought (express or implied) beyond a reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Identity of the killer
issues.why: The State had to prove Sheffield was the perpetrator rather than an unknown third party.

issues.label: Proof of malice/intent
issues.why: The court must decide whether the evidence allowed a rational jury to infer intent to kill or implied malice from circumstances.

issues.label: Circumstantial evidence standard
issues.why: If Georgia’s circumstantial-evidence rule applies, the court must consider whether the evidence excluded every reasonable hypothesis save guilt (as charged to the jury).

issues.label: Sufficiency on motive evidence
issues.why: The court must assess whether evidence of the affair/relationship was properly considered as motive and how it supports guilt without being required.

issues.label: Sufficiency on opportunity
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the timing, Sheffield’s location, and access supported opportunity to commit the shooting and set the fire.

issues.label: Sufficiency on consciousness of guilt
issues.why: The court must consider whether post-fire behavior (lack of inquiry, focus on valuables, phone call conduct) supports an inference of guilt.

issues.label: Sufficiency on arson cover-up theory
issues.why: The court must decide whether the fire evidence permits an inference it was intentionally set to destroy evidence and conceal homicide.

issues.label: Sufficiency despite unknown weapon match
issues.why: The court must determine whether inability to ballistically match the burned shotgun precludes a rational finding of guilt.

issues.label: Sufficiency despite third-party hypotheses
issues.why: The court must address whether the burglary/unknown-men/woods activity created reasonable doubt as a matter of law.

issues.label: Weight vs. legal sufficiency
issues.why: The court must avoid reweighing evidence and distinguish credibility/weight arguments from true legal insufficiency.

issues.label: Constitutional speedy-trial framework
issues.why: The court must analyze the claim under the Sixth Amendment/Georgia Constitution using the Barker v. Wingo factors.

issues.label: Speedy-trial attachment date
issues.why: The court must determine when the right attached (arrest/indictment) and what time periods are legally relevant.

issues.label: Length of post-accusation delay
issues.why: The court must calculate the delay from indictment/arrest to trial and decide whether it is presumptively prejudicial.

issues.label: Reason for the delay
issues.why: The court must assign weight among valid reasons, negligence, or bad faith, including case complexity and investigative needs.

issues.label: Attribution of delay to defendant
issues.why: The court must determine whether continuances, motions, counsel changes, or other defense actions contributed to the delay.

issues.label: Assertion of speedy-trial right
issues.why: The court must evaluate when and how vigorously Sheffield asserted the right and the effect of any delay in asserting it.

issues.label: Prejudice: oppressive incarceration
issues.why: The court must assess prejudice from pretrial detention conditions and length after arrest.

issues.label: Prejudice: anxiety and concern
issues.why: The court must consider evidence of personal anxiety beyond ordinary pending-charge stress.

issues.label: Prejudice: defense impairment
issues.why: The court must determine whether delay impaired the defense through lost witnesses, faded memories, or lost evidence.

issues.label: Presumptive prejudice (Doggett)
issues.why: If delay is long and attributable to the State, the court must consider whether prejudice may be presumed and whether rebutted.

issues.label: Pre-indictment delay due process
issues.why: Given the ~6-year investigation, the court must consider whether any separate due-process claim of prejudicial pre-accusation delay was raised and, if so, its elements.

issues.label: Speedy-trial remedy
issues.why: If a violation is found, the court must apply the required remedy of dismissal with prejudice.

issues.label: Deference to trial court findings
issues.why: For speedy-trial rulings after evidentiary hearings, the court must apply the correct deference to factual findings and credibility determinations.

issues.label: Harmless-error doctrine scope
issues.why: The court must recognize that some errors (e.g., speedy-trial violation) are structural/remedial, while others may be harmless, affecting relief.

issues.label: Other claims in new-trial motion
issues.why: Because Sheffield raised additional claims, the court must identify which are properly presented on appeal and address them if necessary to decide the case correctly.
